title: Natural selection
group: BIO-EVOL / BIO-ECOL / BIO-PLANT — Evolution, Ecology & Plants
examples: Can you explain how natural selection works using an example?
What is the difference between adaptation and natural selection?
How long does natural selection take to cause a change?

explain.say: Natural selection is a process that drives evolution over time.

items: It changes populations over many generations.
It favors traits best suited to an environment.
It is based on existing variation within a species.

explain.say: First, there must be variation among individuals in a population.
Second, organisms produce more offspring than the environment can support.
Third, some variations give individuals a survival advantage in their specific environment.

draw.text: Survival advantage helps traits pass on

explain.say: Finally, those individuals with the best traits are more likely to survive and reproduce.
Consider the peppered moths in industrial areas where soot darkened the trees.

faq.q: Does natural selection create new genes?
faq.a: No, natural selection does not create new genes. It only acts on the variations that already exist within a population.
asks: Where do the variations come from?
Is natural selection a way to make things different?

faq.q: Is natural selection the same as evolution?
faq.a: No, natural selection is the main mechanism or process that causes evolution. Evolution is the overall change in a species over long periods.
asks: What is the difference between evolution and natural selection?
Is natural selection the only way species change?

faq.q: Does the environment choose the traits, or does the trait choose the environment?
faq.a: The environment acts as the selective pressure, choosing which existing traits are best suited for survival at that time.
asks: Who is in charge in natural selection?
Does the organism decide what is best for it?

faq.q: If a trait is helpful now, will it always be helpful?
faq.a: No, the environment changes over time. A trait that was helpful might become unhelpful if the environment changes significantly.
asks: Does selection depend on the time period?

faq.q: How fast does natural selection happen?
faq.a: Natural selection operates over many generations, which can take thousands or millions of years to cause major changes.
asks: Is this process quick or slow?
What is the timescale for evolution?

facts: Variation exists due to random genetic mutations.
Competition for resources drives the need for survival traits.
The fittest individuals are those best suited to the current environment.
Natural selection acts on existing variation, it does not create it.

quiz.say: In a population of beetles, some are green and some are brown. If the background colour is dark soil, which trait gives the best camouflage?

options.show: It depends on the beetle's mood
options.say: It depends on the beetle's mood

quiz.why: Brown beetles blend in better with the dark soil, making them harder for predators to see.

wrong.0: Survival is based on physical traits, not feelings.
wrong.2: Green might seem good, but it stands out too much against dark soil.
wrong.3: The background colour makes one colour significantly better at hiding.

quiz.say: Which step is the core idea of natural selection?
quiz.why: This means some individuals survive and pass on their traits more successfully than others.

wrong.1: Mutation is the source of variation, not the selection process itself.
wrong.2: Competition involves more than just food; it includes predators too.
wrong.3: Selection acts on the whole population, not just one strong animal.

quiz.say: If a species lives in a very cold environment, what is the most likely beneficial variation?
quiz.why: Thicker fur helps the organism retain heat and survive the cold temperatures.

wrong.0: Bright colours are often used for warning, but they might attract predators in the cold.
wrong.1: While size helps, insulation is a more direct adaptation to cold.
wrong.2: Running is useful, but retaining heat is the primary challenge in extreme cold.
